newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault workers hurt in police clash.
newsitem.headline: Renault workers hurt in police clash.

text.p: Four Renault workers were injured on Thursday when strikers from the car company's doomed Belgian plant and police clashed in the northern French city of Lille.
Police said 300 demonstrators protesting against Renault's plan to close the Vilvoorde plant had come to Lille to speak with Mayor Pierre Mauroy, a former Socialist prime minister.
After hearing that Mauroy was in Paris, they threw eggs, broke windows and tried to force their way into city hall, prompting police to intervene.
Four workers were taken to hospital. Three of them were released with slight injuries, police said. A few workers were questioned by police before the group headed back to Belgium in the afternoon.
Renault sparked an outcry when it announced on February 27 that it would close the Vilvoorde plant, which employs 3,100 people, in July to streamline its operations and cut costs.
Vilvoorde workers, who went on strike for six weeks after the announcement, resumed work on April 14 but staged a 24-hour strike on Thursday.
Courts in France and in Belgium have ruled that Renault breached the law in failing to consult staff ahead of the announcement.
